a: Biohacking is the practice of making deliberate, measured changes to lifestyle, environment, nutrition and sometimes supplementation to improve health, performance or longevity — and tracking whether they work. The emphasis on measurement is what separates it from general wellness advice.

Sleep timing, morning light, adequate protein and easy aerobic exercise — in that order — produce the largest measured improvements and cost nothing. Devices and supplements come after those four are in place.

The foundational practices are the same things medicine recommends. Risk rises with unregulated compounds, extreme fasting, and acting on single data points. The Hub grades evidence on every entry so you can see where the research is strong and where it is early.

q: Which supplements are actually worth taking?
a: For most people: creatine, magnesium, omega-3, and vitamin D where a blood test shows deficiency. Everything else needs a specific reason and ideally a marker you can check.
No, but a wearable makes trends visible. Use it for weekly patterns and ignore single nights — a one-off low reading is noise, three days in a row is information.

q: What blood tests should I ask for?
a: Beyond a standard panel: fasting insulin, ApoB, hs-CRP and 25-hydroxyvitamin D. They catch the decade before disease rather than disease itself.
